# mcp-warden rules

<!-- generated by scripts/gen-rules-doc.js – do not edit by hand -->

Severities can be raised or lowered per finding depending on context (for example, auto-approving a `delete_file` tool is high, auto-approving `list_files` is medium).
Disable any rule with `--ignore <ID or name>`.

## Config rules

### MW001

**`hardcoded-secret`** · default severity: **critical**

Hard-coded secret in MCP config.

API keys, tokens or passwords are stored in plain text in the config. Anything that can read the file (other apps, backups, dotfile repos, malicious MCP servers with filesystem access) can steal them.

**How to fix:** Move the value to your OS keychain or a shell environment variable and reference it (e.g. "${env:GITHUB_TOKEN}" in VS Code, or export it before launching the client). Rotate the leaked credential.

### MW002

**`unpinned-package`** · default severity: **medium**

Server package is not pinned to an exact version.

Runners like npx, uvx and docker fetch whatever the registry serves at launch time. A compromised maintainer account or a malicious update is executed automatically, with your user privileges, the next time your AI client starts.

**How to fix:** Pin an exact version (npx -y pkg@1.2.3, uvx pkg==1.2.3) or an image digest (image@sha256:…), and review changes before bumping.

### MW003

**`typosquat`** · default severity: **high**

Package name looks like a typosquat of a popular MCP server.

The package name is one or two characters away from a well-known MCP server or impersonates a trusted npm scope. Typosquatted MCP servers have been used to exfiltrate credentials and inject instructions into AI agents.

**How to fix:** Double-check the exact package name against the vendor's official documentation before running it.

### MW004

**`archived-server`** · default severity: **medium**

Server package is archived and unmaintained.

This reference server was moved to modelcontextprotocol/servers-archived and no longer receives security fixes.

**How to fix:** Switch to the vendor-maintained replacement and remove the archived package.

### MW005

**`insecure-transport`** · default severity: **high**

Remote MCP server over unencrypted HTTP.

Traffic (including tool calls, results and any auth headers) to a non-local server is sent in clear text and can be read or modified by anyone on the network path.

**How to fix:** Use an https:// endpoint. Plain http is only acceptable for localhost.

### MW006

**`shell-execution`** · default severity: **high**

Server is launched through a shell command string.

Launching via "sh -c" / "cmd /c" with a command string hides what actually runs, enables injection through environment variables and makes the config hard to review.

**How to fix:** Invoke the server binary directly with an explicit "command" and "args" array.

### MW007

**`remote-code-download`** · default severity: **critical**

Downloads and executes remote code at launch.

The server pipes a script from the internet into an interpreter (curl | sh, iwr | iex …). Whoever controls that URL controls your machine every time the AI client starts.

**How to fix:** Install the server once from a reviewed, pinned release and launch the local binary.

### MW008

**`dangerous-container`** · default severity: **high**

Container runs with dangerous privileges.

Docker flags such as --privileged, a mounted Docker socket or host namespaces let a compromised MCP server escape the container and take over the host.

**How to fix:** Drop --privileged, never mount /var/run/docker.sock, avoid --network/--pid host, and mount only the directories the server needs (read-only where possible).

### MW009

**`broad-filesystem-access`** · default severity: **high**

Server is granted access to the entire disk or home directory.

Giving an MCP server "/" or your whole home directory exposes SSH keys, cloud credentials, browser profiles and other AI-client configs to any prompt-injected tool call.

**How to fix:** Grant only the specific project directories the server needs.

### MW010

**`secret-in-url`** · default severity: **high**

Credential embedded in a URL.

Tokens in URLs leak through logs, proxies, browser history and error messages.

**How to fix:** Send credentials in an Authorization header sourced from an environment variable.

### MW011

**`auto-approve`** · default severity: **medium**

Tool calls are auto-approved.

Auto-approving tools removes the human confirmation step that protects you from prompt injection. A malicious web page or document can then make the agent call these tools silently.

**How to fix:** Remove alwaysAllow/autoApprove entries (or "trust": true) for tools that write, delete, send or execute.

### MW012

**`privilege-escalation`** · default severity: **high**

Server runs with elevated privileges.

Running an MCP server as root/administrator means a single prompt-injected tool call can modify the whole system.

**How to fix:** Run the server as your normal user; grant narrowly-scoped permissions instead.

### MW013

**`inline-code`** · default severity: **medium**

Server launches inline interpreter code.

Inline code (node -e, python -c, deno eval) is hard to audit and is a common way to smuggle loaders into configs.

**How to fix:** Put the code in a reviewed file in your repository and launch that file.

### MW014

**`tls-verification-disabled`** · default severity: **high**

TLS certificate verification is disabled.

Disabling certificate checks lets anyone on the network impersonate the API the server talks to and capture its credentials.

**How to fix:** Remove the override. If you need a corporate CA, point NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS / SSL_CERT_FILE at it instead.

### MW015

**`untrusted-registry`** · default severity: **medium**

Packages are installed from a non-default registry.

A custom or plain-HTTP package index can serve modified packages. Make sure the registry is one you control and trust.

**How to fix:** Use the default registry or a verified internal mirror over HTTPS.

### MW016

**`remote-without-auth`** · default severity: **info**

Remote MCP server configured without credentials.

No Authorization header is configured. That is fine for servers that use OAuth (the client will prompt), but double-check the endpoint is the vendor's official one.

**How to fix:** Verify the server URL against the vendor documentation.

### MW019

**`known-vulnerable-package`** · default severity: **critical**

Server package has a known vulnerability or is malicious.

The configured package (or version) is affected by a published vulnerability or was identified as malicious.

**How to fix:** Upgrade to the fixed version and pin it, or remove the package entirely if it is marked malicious.

### MW017

**`config-permissions`** · default severity: **medium**

Config containing secrets is readable by other users.

The file holds credentials but is group- or world-readable.

**How to fix:** chmod 600 the file (and better: move the secrets out of it).

### MW018

**`duplicate-key-shadowing`** · default severity: **high**

Duplicate key hides a different server definition.

JSON parsers keep the LAST value of a duplicated key. A config can show reviewers a harmless server (or "command") near the top while the client actually loads a different one defined later under the same name.

**How to fix:** Remove the duplicate so every server name and field appears exactly once, and check which definition your client was actually running.

## Tool-poisoning rules

### TP001

**`hidden-instructions`** · default severity: **high**

Tool description contains instructions aimed at the model.

**How to fix:** Tool descriptions should describe behaviour, not command the assistant. Remove or replace this server.

### TP002

**`concealment`** · default severity: **critical**

Tool asks the model to hide actions from the user.

**How to fix:** Treat the server as malicious. Remove it and rotate any credentials it could have seen.

### TP003

**`sensitive-file-access`** · default severity: **high**

Tool description references credential or config files.

**How to fix:** A legitimate tool rarely needs to mention SSH keys or other AI-client configs in its description. Investigate before use.

### TP004

**`invisible-characters`** · default severity: **high**

Tool metadata contains invisible, control or bidirectional characters.

**How to fix:** Invisible characters and terminal escape sequences can carry instructions humans cannot see, or rewrite what your terminal shows. Strip them or remove the server.

### TP005

**`tool-shadowing`** · default severity: **medium**

Tool tries to influence how other tools are used.

**How to fix:** A tool should not change the behaviour of other tools. This is a classic cross-server shadowing attack.

### TP006

**`exfiltration-channel`** · default severity: **medium**

Tool description embeds URLs or encoded data.

**How to fix:** Check where the URL points and why a description needs it. Long encoded blobs are a common way to hide payloads.

### TP007

**`oversized-description`** · default severity: **low**

Unusually long tool description.

**How to fix:** Very long descriptions consume context and are often used to bury instructions. Review the full text.

### TP008

**`secret-in-tool`** · default severity: **high**

Tool metadata contains a credential.

**How to fix:** The server is leaking a credential to every client and model that lists its tools. Report it to the maintainer.

### TP009

**`context-smuggling-parameter`** · default severity: **medium**

Tool requests conversation or system context as a parameter.

### TP010

**`tool-name-collision`** · default severity: **medium**

Same tool name exposed by multiple servers.

### TP011

**`tool-definition-changed`** · default severity: **high**

Tool definition changed since it was pinned (possible rug pull).

A server changed the description or schema of a tool after you pinned it with --lock. Malicious servers can behave well during review and change their tool descriptions later.

**How to fix:** Diff the definition, then run with --update-lock once reviewed.

### TP012

**`tool-removed`** · default severity: **info**

Pinned tool no longer exposed.

**How to fix:** Run with --update-lock to accept the change.

### TP013

**`tool-added`** · default severity: **low**

New server or tool not present in the lock file.

**How to fix:** Review the new tool, then run with --update-lock to pin it.
